# Backchannel v0.5.2

v0.5.1 was tagged but never distributed: its desktop bundles were not published,
so no installation ever ran it. This release supersedes it and carries all of its
changes. If you are coming from v0.5.0, read the v0.5.1 notes alongside these.

## Highlights

- **Briefing headings get the width of their card.** In the post-call briefing,
  each item's title shared a line with its status and speaker labels. In the
  three-across cards at the bottom -- objectives, opportunities, open questions
  -- those labels claimed most of the available width and left a five-word
  heading wrapping over five lines beside a mostly empty card. The labels now
  drop to their own line when there is no longer room beside the title, so a
  heading reads as a heading. Cards with room to spare are unchanged.

## Carried from v0.5.1

Everything in that release ships here for the first time: the Tokens tab
reporting what a call cost rather than counting tokens, including the live audio
bridge that is billed per minute and previously showed nothing; suppression of
duplicate transcript entries on calls that capture both microphone and meeting
audio; bounded analysis replies; lighter processor use during a call; the
clearer meeting-audio option on the pre-call screen; GPT Live Transcribe and
Gemini 3.7 Flash; corrected Gemini Flash pricing; and the fix for insights that
could be deleted by being merged into themselves.

## Upgrading

No action required. Sessions, agents, documents, and endpoint configuration
carry forward. The usage table gains a column for audio duration, applied
automatically on first start. Historical sessions are not rewritten, so a call
recorded before this release still shows nothing for the live audio bridge.
Desktop installs on v0.5.0 update in place through the in-app updater.

## Included

The release coordinator's documented invocation now also covers running it from
a bash shell, where the PowerShell call operator does not parse. That correction
had previously cost a cycle on two separate releases while living only in
operator memory.
